new_public_evidence.source: Shaer, Bar, Prinster & Romano (2026), Testing For Distribution Shifts with Conditional Conformal Test Martingales, arXiv:2602.13848v2
new_public_evidence.result: Directly treats a fixed finite null reference set plus an indefinitely growing test stream. The conditional CTM never adds test points to the reference set; it corrects finite-reference ECDF error with a confidence band and yields finite-sample anytime type-I control conditional on the reference event, plus asymptotic-power and expected-delay results when the resulting ECDF-mean signal clears the correction.

new_public_evidence.source: Turner, Ly & Grünwald (2024), Generic E-variables for exact sequential k-sample tests that allow for optional stopping
new_public_evidence.result: Formula-level reread narrows the previous route: the sequential block product requires fresh positive group sizes in each completed block. It does not directly license repeatedly reusing one frozen finite baseline sample while only the post group grows. For a simple Gaussian alternative the generic block denominator is also not generally reducible to only count/sum/sum_sq.

new_public_evidence.source: Hao, Grünwald, Lardy, Long & Adams (2024), E-values for k-Sample Tests with Exponential Families
new_public_evidence.result: The formal tractable theory is stated for regular one-dimensional exponential families and the explicit Gaussian result is location-only with fixed variance. This does not close the full unknown-mean-and-variance frozen-reference Gaussian problem.

derived_results.claim: For the late-start structural problem, conditional conformal test martingales are a materially better match than the Turner/Hao block route because they explicitly permit a fixed finite reference set and only the incoming stream grows forever.
derived_results.scope: General distribution-shift testing with a fixed score function; guarantee is conditional/high-probability over the finite reference calibration event and must be budgeted with that calibration failure probability.

derived_results.claim: In the standardized Gaussian setting P=N(0,1), two fixed score channels s1(x)=x and s2(x)=x^2 numerically appear to cover every Gaussian alternative on the exact KL=1 boundary with a nonzero ECDF-mean signal.

details.radial_scan: A numerical global scan over information levels I in [1,20] found the minimum at I=1 and no material nonmonotonic decrease; the optimized minimum rises toward about 1/6 for large I.

derived_results.claim: With reference n=684 and two conditional-CTM channels each assigned alpha=0.02 and calibration delta=0.005, a union-bound global false-alarm budget is at most 0.05 without requiring channel independence. DKW epsilon per channel is about 0.0661795, so a conservative effective-signal proxy is 0.1643729-2*epsilon ~= 0.0320139 >0. The corresponding n threshold for 2*sqrt(log(2/delta)/(2n)) < 0.1643729 is 444.
derived_results.scope: Uses the numerical KL>=1 signal-floor candidate and constant DKW band; it is not yet a proof of power over the full Gaussian KL>=1 continuum.

derived_results.claim: A promising bounded-state architecture is to retain the existing finite-prefix t/F sentinel for early high-power detection and add two fixed-reference conditional-CTM channels on x and x^2 as an indefinite noncontaminating late fallback. Dynamic monitoring state is constant-size apart from the fixed reference score arrays; ECDF lookup can be logarithmic per sample after sorting.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The raw x-score conditional CTM alone has no asymptotic mean-bet signal against symmetric pure variance changes because E[Phi(Y)]=1/2 when Y is centered and symmetric; a second magnitude-sensitive score is required.

Turner/Hao sequential k-sample constructions should not be used to justify repeatedly recycling the exact same frozen baseline observations in every new block unless a separate conditional-validity argument is supplied.

If standardization parameters are learned from the same reference used for calibration, fixed-score conditional-CTM theory cannot be assumed unchanged. A safe generic implementation would use externally fixed scores or split reference data into fit and calibration portions and condition on the fitted score map.
The 0.1643728991 signal floor and its apparent radial monotonicity are numerical findings, not interval-certified theorems.

candidate_new.mechanism: Run two Shaer-et-al.-style conditional CTMs against the same frozen Gaussian reference, using fixed scores x and x^2 and disjoint alpha/delta budgets. Combine by union bound, not by multiplying dependent wealths. Keep the existing first-start t/F sentinel as an early channel. This avoids start-index alpha dilution and test-time reference contamination while retaining sensitivity to both mean and variance shifts.
candidate_new.main_blocker: Need a rigorous continuum lower bound for max{a(mu,r),b(mu,r)} over all Gaussian alternatives with KL>=1, preferably interval/direct-rounding certified, and then a matched-delay comparison against the existing sentinel/SNML channel under one global PFA budget.

frontier: Prove or interval-certify inf_{D_KL(N(mu,r)||N(0,1))>=1} max{a(mu,r),b(mu,r)} >= 0.1643 (or a slightly weaker robust constant). Separate exact KL=1 angular coverage from radial extension and do not infer the latter solely from numerical scans.

Translate that certified signal floor through Shaer et al.'s exact betting constants/ONS theorem, not only the DKW heuristic, to obtain a finite expected-delay or high-probability delay bound for the two-channel detector at n=684.

Match the two-channel conditional-CTM alpha/delta budget against the r77 t/F sentinel and current SNML future-tail channel and compare delay/power on common-random Gaussian paths across mixed mean/variance directions.

For unknown baseline scaling, derive a reference split (fit score transform on one part, calibrate ECDF on an independent part) and account for the resulting smaller calibration n before claiming full unknown-mean/variance applicability.
Keep Turner/Hao as alternative k-sample tools only when fresh observations are available in every group; do not use them as the frozen-reference proof.
exact_next_action: Interval-certify the two-score Gaussian population signal floor over KL>=1, beginning with the exact KL=1 boundary and then a radial enclosure. If a robust floor survives, plug it into the conditional-CTM theorem with the actual n=684 alpha/delta split and derive a formal delay certificate; if it fails, add a third fixed score or retain conditional CTM only as a partial late-fallback channel.
